section_title: Manner in which complaint shall be made
text: A consumer complaint about goods sold/delivered (or agreed to be) or a service provided (or agreed to be), or an allegation of unfair trade practice, may be filed with the District Commission. It may be filed by the affected consumer, a recognised consumer association (whether or not the consumer is a member), one or more consumers representing others with the same interest (with District Commission permission), or the Central/State Government. Complaints may be filed electronically and must include the prescribed fee.

Consumer complaints are routed by claim value (based on consideration paid, not compensation claimed). Per the Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction of the District Commission, the State Commission and the National Commission) Rules, 2021, which revised the original 2019 Act limits: the District Commission handles claims up to Rs 50 lakh, the State Commission handles claims above Rs 50 lakh up to Rs 2 crore, and the National Commission (NCDRC) handles claims exceeding Rs 2 crore.

section: Section 59 (formerly Section 33C, Industrial Disputes Act 1947 - superseded 21 Nov 2025)
section_title: Recovery of money due from an employer
text: Where money is due to a worker from an employer under a settlement, award, or specified chapters of the Code, the worker (or an authorised person, or heirs if deceased) may apply to the appropriate Government for recovery. If satisfied the amount is due, the Government issues a recovery certificate to the Collector, who recovers it as an arrear of land revenue. The application must generally be made within one year of the money becoming due. Multiple workers owed money by the same employer may file jointly. Note: this provision carries forward the erstwhile Section 33C of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, which stood superseded when the Industrial Relations Code, 2020 came into force on 21 November 2025.

section_title: Claims for underpayment of minimum wages
text: Provides a mechanism for an employee to file a claim before the designated authority when paid less than the minimum wage fixed for their scheduled employment, allowing recovery of the shortfall. Note: check current status, as Wage Code, 2019 provisions on minimum wages have also come into force alongside the Industrial Relations Code as part of the 2025-26 Labour Codes rollout.

section: Section 144 (formerly Section 125, CrPC 1973, effective till 30 June 2024)
section_title: Order for maintenance of wives, children and parents
text: If any person having sufficient means neglects or refuses to maintain his wife (unable to maintain herself), his legitimate or illegitimate minor child, a child who has attained majority but is unable to maintain themselves due to physical/mental abnormality or injury, or his father or mother unable to maintain themselves, a Magistrate of the First Class may order him to pay a monthly allowance for their maintenance. Effective 1 July 2024, this provision replaced Section 125 of the CrPC, 1973, and carries forward the same rights and case law.

section_title: Establishment and jurisdiction of Family Courts
text: Establishes Family Courts to promote conciliation and secure speedy settlement of disputes relating to marriage and family affairs, including maintenance, custody, and matrimonial relief.

act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
text: An aggrieved person, a Protection Officer, or any other person on her behalf may present an application to the Magistrate seeking one or more reliefs under the Act (protection, residence, monetary relief, custody, compensation). Before ordering relief, the Magistrate considers any Domestic Incident Report from the Protection Officer or service provider. Applications may be filed before a Judicial Magistrate of the First Class or Metropolitan Magistrate with jurisdiction where the aggrieved person resides, works, or where the cause of action arose. The Magistrate is directed to try and dispose of the application within 60 days from the first hearing.

act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
section_title: Residence, monetary relief, and custody orders
text: The Magistrate can pass a residence order directing the respondent to leave the shared household, a monetary relief order to cover the aggrieved person's and children's expenses and losses from domestic violence, and a temporary custody order for any children in favour of the aggrieved person.

section: General (recovery of possession, declaratory and injunctive relief)
text: Provides remedies for recovery of possession of immovable property, declaration of title/rights, and preventive relief through injunctions. Used for boundary disputes, encroachment, and disputes over possession or ownership between private parties, which must be adjudicated by the competent Civil Court.

section_title: Mutation records and encroachment on government land
text: Governs maintenance of land records, mutation (khata transfer) after a change in ownership or possession, and land revenue collection. Mutation only updates who pays land revenue and carries no presumptive value on legal title; a genuine title/possession dispute between private parties must go to the civil court, not the revenue authority. Under Section 104, for encroachment on government land, the Tahsildar can summarily evict unauthorised occupants.

section_title: Criteria for free legal aid eligibility
text: A person is entitled to free legal services if they are: a member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe; a victim of trafficking in human beings or begar; a woman or child (irrespective of income); a person with disability; a victim of a mass disaster, ethnic violence, caste atrocity, flood, drought, earthquake or industrial disaster; an industrial workman; a person in custody (including protective or juvenile homes, or a psychiatric institution); or a person whose annual income is below the limit prescribed by the concerned State Government (or below Rs 5 lakh for Supreme Court matters).

Persons who satisfy the Section 12 criteria are entitled to receive legal services, provided the concerned Legal Services Authority is satisfied that the person has a prima facie case to prosecute or defend. An affidavit as to income may be treated as sufficient proof of eligibility unless the Authority has reason to disbelieve it.

section_title: Lok Adalat for amicable dispute settlement
text: The Act promotes the organisation of Lok Adalats for amicable settlement of disputes that are pending in court or at a pre-litigation stage, offering a faster, informal, and free alternative dispute resolution route for grievances that do not clearly fit one specific statutory category.
